title: Operator efficiency probe: task-switching, cost visibility & quick-rollouts (Oct 2026)
summary: Concise synthesis of a 5-session moderated usability probe with operators and platform engineers focused on task-switching costs, visibility into per-route token spend, and the friction of creating quick rollouts. Goal: identify 2–3 high-impact UI changes that reduce cognitive load and time-to-complete for common admin tasks.
participants: 5 participants (3 platform engineers at startups, 2 SREs at mid-market customers). Sessions remotely moderated; each ~45 minutes. Participants recruited from recent beta users of canary rollouts and cost dashboards.
methods: Think-aloud task scenarios; high-fidelity wireframe click-throughs (v2 and v3); time-to-task measurements; qualitative post-task probe. Tasks: create a canary rollout with 10% traffic, inspect per-route token cost for previous 24h, revert a rollout to baseline.
findings: 1) Task switching costs are high when context is not preserved. Participants repeatedly lost which route they were editing after drilling into cost details. 2) Cost visibility (per-route token/latency) is trusted when time range and model variant are explicit; confusion arises when mix of model-variants rolled up under a single route. 3) Quick-rollout flow felt 'too modal' — participants disliked being forced into a multi-step modal with limited access to related route metadata. 4) Participants wanted an inline 'preview impact' that estimates token cost delta before committing rollout changes (preferably with toggle between 1h/24h/7d projections). 5) Error recovery: reverting a rollout took extra clicks; participants expected undo-style affordances or a single-click fallback linked from the route-level toolbar. 6) Wireframe v3 (side-panel + preserved header) reduced average task time by ~18% vs v2 (full-screen modal), mainly by preserving route context and breadcrumbs.
notable-quotes: "I keep losing track of what model was in that route — are we looking at 'chat-l' or 'chat-l-quant'?"
"It feels like I'm leaving the route page every time I check cost — I want a quick snapshot inline."
"An estimate of how much this will cost us would save a support ticket later."
wireframes: v2: full-screen modal flow for rollouts; v3: right-side docked panel that overlays the route list and preserves breadcrumbs. Cost preview widget mockups included: compact and expanded states, toggle time-range, projection slider. Prototype links in linked_artifacts. Key microcopy iterations: clarify 'model variant' vs 'serving variant'.
backlog_actions: Add route-level persistent banner showing active rollouts and model variants (owner: product; priority: P1)
Prototype and run A/B test for side-panel rollout UI (owner: ux-engineering; priority: P1)
Design inline cost preview (1h/24h/7d) and add toggle for 'estimate mode' (owner: platform; priority: P2)
Add single-click 'fallback' button on route toolbar that reverts to last-stable rollout (owner: serving-runtime; priority: P2)
Update data model to explicitly associate per-request tokens with serving variant for accurate rollups (owner: infra; priority: P1)
open_questions: How granular should cost projections be for private deployments with varying dedicated allocations?
Do legal/compliance teams require persisted audit events for preview-estimates (possible leakage concerns)?
Is there an appetite for exposing 'estimated dollar impact' for customers on committed reserved capacity?
next_steps: Schedule design sprint week (Oct 18–22) to flush out v4 wireframes and hi-fi prototypes
Align infra owners on data adjustments by Oct 15 (blocking for accurate rollups)
Run 3 quick unmoderated tests with v3 side-panel focusing on revert flow and cost preview wording
Prepare a short customer-facing one-pager summarizing proposed UX changes for enterprise customers (owner: solutions-eng)
